summary: A 1937 CCC-built L-4 tower above Sheep Creek Canyon, one of only two lookouts left in Utah and the only one with living quarters above ground.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 32-foot timber tower, with catwalk

access.note: Open for Forest Service-run interpretive tours Fridays and Saturdays in season; reached by a drivable gravel road off the Sheep Creek Canyon Geologic Loop.

visit.trail_note: Drive-up via gravel road, about 2.5 miles off the Sheep Creek Canyon Geologic Loop toward Spirit Lake; a hiking approach from Browne Lake is also possible.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Ashley National Forest, Flaming Gorge Ranger District

events.note: Built by the Sheep Creek Canyon CCC camp.
NHLR gives 1968 as the last year staffed; a 2015 newspaper account instead gives 1969, attributing the closure to rot in the tower's legs.
Nominated in 1978 (per NHLR); listed April 10, 1980, reference 80003895 (per Wikipedia/Wikidata; NHLR does not give the listing date or reference number).

NHLR dates this restoration (by USFS and partner organizations) to 1986; a 2015 newspaper account instead describes an early-1980s renovation reopening to the public in 1987. The two accounts disagree on the year.
Registered as US 261 / UT 1 on March 1, 1998.
Closed in 2008 after structural deterioration was found, then restored and rededicated September 20, 2014.

corrections.proposed: Flag as disputed: Wikipedia, Wikidata and willhiteweb all give 8,834 ft, not 8,819 ft.
corrections.evidence: NHLR's cached page lists 'Elevation 8,819 ft (2,688 m)'; Wikipedia/Wikidata infoboxes and willhiteweb's page ('Summit Elevation: 8,834 feet') all give 8,834 ft instead.

sources.title: Renovated fire lookout tower open for tours in Daggett County

notes_for_editor: Two small date conflicts in the sources, both noted in the story rather than resolved: last staffed year (NHLR: 1968; Deseret News: 1969) and the restoration year before the 2008 closure (NHLR: 1986; Deseret News: early-1980s renovation, reopened 1987). Nothing in hand to adjudicate either. The record itself checks out against all sources on name, location, build year (1937) and status. The tower is now a staffed-by-volunteers interpretive/tour site rather than an active detection post, which the current record's staffing/access/visit fields didn't yet reflect. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found a third, previously unflagged conflict: NHLR gives elevation as 8,819 ft, but Wikipedia, Wikidata and willhiteweb all give 8,834 ft; now flagged in the story and as a correction above rather than resolved. Also corrected three footnote misattributions in the original story/JSON draft: the '360 square miles' view figure and the above-ground-living-quarters uniqueness claim were cited partly to NHLR, which does not state either; and the NRHP listing date/reference number was cited partly to NHLR, which gives only the 1978 nomination, not the 1980 listing date or reference number. Willhiteweb separately gives a 1935 build year, at odds with the 1937 given by NHLR, Wikipedia, Wikidata and Deseret News; left unflagged since the story never cites willhiteweb for the build year and the other four sources agree. Also fixed a pronoun error: the story referred to the current volunteer tour guide as 'him', but the cited Deseret News source names her as Clare Boerigter ('her third season').
